OSPS-AC-01.01.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member and accepts only secure methods, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

OSPS-AC-02.01.justification: A new member gets read access, the organization's base permission (gh api orgs/btclib-org --jq .default_repository_permission). Every higher grant is assigned by hand, through an issue in btclib-org/.github that an owner other than the one asking approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made

OSPS-AC-03.01.justification: The main-self-merge ruleset requires a pull request for every change to main. Its one bypass actor holds it in pull_request mode, which never allows a direct push. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-03.02.justification: The main-integrity ruleset forbids deleting main and has no bypass actor. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-AC-04.01.justification: The default GITHUB_TOKEN is read-only at the organization and the repository, and cannot approve pull requests. Every workflow also sets permissions: contents: read at the top. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-AC-04.02.justification: Every workflow sets permissions: contents: read at the top, and a job adds a write scope only where it uses it. zizmor's excessive-permissions audit runs in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#what-every-workflow-does

OSPS-BR-01.01.justification: No workflow uses pull_request_target or workflow_run. Event fields and inputs reach run: steps only through env:, and zizmor's template-injection audit in the required lint check refuses the unsafe form. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

OSPS-BR-01.03.justification: Pull-request runs use the pull_request and pull_request_review_comment triggers, which give a fork no secrets and a read-only token. The review job, which holds a secret, runs only when the head repository is this one. On issue_comment, the mention job, which holds a secret on any pull request, checks out the default branch. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/workflows/reusable-claude-review.yml

OSPS-BR-01.04.justification: No workflow_dispatch takes an input. A release tag's name reaches steps only through env:, and is checked against the package version before the release is built. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml

OSPS-BR-02.01.justification: Each release has a unique version: libsecp256k1's M.N.P, plus a fourth number for a release of the bindings alone, set by a v* tag. release.yml refuses a tag that differs from the package version or is not on main, and PyPI never accepts a version twice. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases

OSPS-BR-02.02.justification: Every release file carries the version in its name: the sdist and the wheels on PyPI, and the CycloneDX SBOM and the attestation bundle on the GitHub release. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-03.01.justification: Every official channel the project lists is served over HTTPS only: the GitHub repository, its issue tracker and advisories, and the documentation at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io.

OSPS-BR-03.02.justification: Releases are distributed through PyPI and GitHub Releases, both HTTPS only. PyPI files carry PEP 740 attestations and the GitHub release a Sigstore bundle. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/

OSPS-BR-04.01.justification: Every release has a CHANGELOG.md entry, listing every change, and a RELEASE_NOTES.md entry, listing what a user must act on, breaking and security changes included. The GitHub release body is the release notes. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

OSPS-BR-05.01.justification: Python dependencies come from PyPI, and the required test check runs the suite with uv from the committed uv.lock with --locked. Every build that ships takes its build requirements from build-constraints.txt, exported from uv.lock with hashes. pre-commit installs its hooks at the revisions .pre-commit-config.yaml names. Third-party actions are pinned by commit SHA. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#uvlock

OSPS-BR-06.01.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing. Every GitHub release from v0.8.0 on carries a Sigstore build-provenance bundle for its sdist. Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest

OSPS-BR-07.01.justification: Secret scanning and push protection are on, so a push carrying a recognised credential is refused. The detect-private-key and detect-secrets hooks run in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.secrets.baseline

OSPS-BR-07.02.justification: A secret is an environment secret that only the owners reach. A secret kept in any other store is recorded in the REPOSITORY.md of the repository that uses it, and btclib-org/.github's tests/secrets_test.py refuses an unrecorded one. A secret is rotated when an owner changes or an exposure is suspected. The secrets kept outside an environment are rotated before they are a year old, and the list is reviewed yearly. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-DO-01.01.justification: The user documentation is README.md's Quickstart, which tests/examples_test.py runs, plus the API reference rendered from the docstrings at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io.

OSPS-DO-02.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md says where a defect is filed, and the bug-report form asks for what a report needs. SECURITY.md sends a vulnerability to a private channel instead. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml

OSPS-DO-03.01.justification: SECURITY.md gives the gh attestation verify command for the release assets, and RELEASING.md the check that rebuilds the sdist from its tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-03.02.justification: The verify command pins the signer: --repo names this repository, --signer-workflow the workflow that signed, which SECURITY.md names for each release, and --source-ref the release tag. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-04.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, and nothing is backported. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-05.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Supported versions*: only the latest release is supported, so a release stops receiving security updates when the next one is published. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

OSPS-DO-06.01.justification: pyproject.toml gives the reason for each runtime dependency. uv obtains them from PyPI and pins them in uv.lock, and Dependabot tracks them weekly with a seven-day cooldown. The vendored C libraries are git submodules pinned by commit, which Dependabot also tracks. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#dependabot-and-pre-commitci

OSPS-DO-07.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the build: uv and a C toolchain are the prerequisites, git submodule update --init fetches the vendored libraries, and uv sync --locked builds the environment and the extension. README.md's *Build* says what each platform needs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-01.01.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's Roles names who holds access to sensitive resources. fametrano is the maintainer and the only bypass actor. Every owner, named there by login, is an administrator of every repository and a reviewer of the publishing environments. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-01.02.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-GV-02.01.justification: Proposed changes and usage questions are discussed publicly in the repository's issues, which have a question form, and pull requests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues

OSPS-GV-03.01.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the contribution process: one subject per pull request, the local gates, the review and the landing. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-03.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states what a contribution must meet: one subject, a Signed-off-by trailer on every commit, the gates CI runs, 100% line and branch coverage, tests against external vectors, and a review against REVIEWING.md. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-GV-04.01.justification: A grant of write or admin, to any repository of the organization, is an issue in btclib-org/.github that states the reason, and an owner other than the one asking approves it there. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#how-a-decision-is-made

OSPS-LE-01.01.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer, Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's aside. Web commits are signed off automatically. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

OSPS-LE-02.01.justification: The source code is under the MIT license, which the OSI approves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-02.02.justification: The released wheels and sdist declare License-Expression: MIT, the same OSI-approved license as the source. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/

OSPS-LE-03.01.justification: The license text is the repository's root LICENSE file. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/LICENSE

OSPS-LE-03.02.justification: LICENSE ships at the sdist root and in every wheel's .dist-info/licenses/. From v0.8.0.10 on, each wheel also carries libsecp256k1's COPYING, and the sdist carries the COPYING of both vendored libraries. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/#files

OSPS-QA-01.01.justification: The repository is public on GitHub at a static URL. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1

OSPS-QA-01.02.justification: Git history on GitHub records every change with its author, committer, date and signature. main refuses force-pushes and requires linear history. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/commits/main

OSPS-QA-02.01.justification: pyproject.toml declares the direct dependencies, the runtime one and the development groups, and the committed uv.lock resolves and pins them. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-02.02.justification: Every release from v0.8.0.7 on attaches a CycloneDX SBOM of the sdist, covered by the release attestation. Every wheel from v0.8.0.10 on carries its own, at .dist-info/sboms/btclib_secp256k1.cdx.json. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest

OSPS-QA-03.01.justification: main requires the six CI status checks. enforce_admins is off, so an admin merge without them is a manual bypass, which the control allows. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-QA-04.01.justification: The organization standard's *Which repositories, and how far* lists every btclib-org repository and its tier. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#which-repositories-and-how-far

OSPS-QA-04.02.justification: libsecp256k1 comes from bitcoin-core/secp256k1, which this project does not administer. The sdist also ships secp256k1-zkp from the fork fametrano/secp256k1-zkp, and no wheel carries it. The fork's branches are unprotected, so what ships is the one commit the submodule pins by sha, and the pin moves only through a pull request here, under main's rules. Every publish job needs zkp-pin. It checks that the pinned commit is the one README.md names and documents, that it is at most one commit ahead of BlockstreamResearch/secp256k1-zkp's master, and that every commit ahead carries a valid signature from fametrano's or Andrew Poelstra's key. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/zkp-pin.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.gitmodules

OSPS-QA-05.01.justification: No generated executable is committed. The only binary files are fuzz seed inputs and the Sphinx inventory python.inv. The vendored C libraries are git submodules of source. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1

OSPS-QA-05.02.justification: The only binary files are fuzz seeds under fuzz/corpus, each an input the library parses, which tests/fuzz_corpus_test.py checks, and docs/source/_inventories/python.inv, whose fetch command docs/source/conf.py gives. None is code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/fuzz/corpus

OSPS-QA-06.01.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every pull request, and its aggregate check, 'test: every job passed', is required on main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

OSPS-QA-06.02.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives the command that runs the tests and says which workflows run them and which gate a merge. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

OSPS-QA-06.03.justification: The policy is 100% line and branch coverage (CONTRIBUTING.md; standard section 8). pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100, so untested new code fails the required test check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

OSPS-QA-07.01.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, but fametrano remains a pull_request-mode bypass actor, so the repository still allows a merge without that approval. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

OSPS-SA-01.01.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents each component, the cffi boundary and the release provenance. ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* and *Trust boundaries* name the actors and what each can do. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

OSPS-SA-02.01.justification: The API reference at https://btclib-secp256k1.readthedocs.io is generated from the docstrings of every public module, and tests/docs_test.py fails when a shipped module is missing from it. ARCHITECTURE.md's *The public surface* states what is public.

OSPS-SA-03.01.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md is the security assessment: claims, threat model, trust boundaries and how each common weakness is countered. SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* records the known residual risks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-SA-03.02.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Threat model* names what is defended, the adversaries and what is not defended. Its *Trust boundaries* maps where untrusted input enters. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

OSPS-VM-01.01.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels, a GitHub security advisory or email, and the timeframes: a report is acknowledged within 7 days, and a fix or a published advisory follows within 90 days. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability

OSPS-VM-02.01.justification: SECURITY.md names the security contacts: a private GitHub security advisory, or email to security at btclib dot org. GOVERNANCE.md's Roles says that address reaches every organization owner. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md#reporting-a-vulnerability https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

OSPS-VM-03.01.justification: Private vulnerability reporting is enabled, and SECURITY.md points to it (the Security tab's 'Report a vulnerability') and gives an email address as the alternative. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories/new

OSPS-VM-04.01.justification: Vulnerabilities are published as GitHub security advisories on this repository: GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, fixed in 0.8.0.10. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories

OSPS-VM-04.02.justification: The CycloneDX SBOM a release attaches lists, in its vulnerabilities array, every vulnerability that the tree's .github/vex.toml judges not to affect the release, with the reason. A tree with no such judgement has no vex.toml, and its SBOM has no vulnerabilities key. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing

OSPS-VM-05.01.justification: The standard sets the threshold: actions/dependency-review-action fails a pull request that adds or changes a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or with a licence outside the allow-list. Its settings are one file, btclib-org/.github's .github/dependency-review.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/dependency-review.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-VM-05.02.justification: release.yml runs uv audit over every dependency the wheel declares, and every publish job needs it to succeed. An advisory, or a service it cannot reach, stops the release. The only exemption is an id that the tree's own .github/vex.toml, carried into the release's signed SBOM, states as not affecting it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing

OSPS-VM-05.03.justification: The required lint check audits the whole uv.lock, every dependency group, on every pull request: check_audit.py --all-groups runs uv audit, which reads OSV's malicious-package (MAL-) entries as well as advisories. Any such entry fails the check, and so does an OSV that cannot be reached. The audit's only exemption is a .github/vex.toml entry, reviewed like any other change. The required Dependency review check also blocks a change that adds a dependency with an advisory of moderate severity or above, or a licence outside the allow-list. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#12-releasing https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#tokens-publishing-scanning

OSPS-VM-06.01.justification: The standard's section 5 sets a threshold of zero for ruff: select = ALL, bandit's S rules included, and each finding is fixed or suppressed in place with a reason. zizmor holds workflows to the same, in the required lint check. CodeQL runs on every pull request, but the standard sets no threshold for its alerts. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#5-ruff

OSPS-VM-06.02.justification: The required lint check runs .pre-commit-config.yaml on every pull request (ruff with the S rules, strict mypy, zizmor, detect-secrets) and blocks the merge on any finding not suppressed in place with a reason. CodeQL also runs on every pull request but is not a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/lint.yml

access_continuity.justification: The organization has three owners, fametrano, giacomocaironi and pmazzocchi, each an administrator of this repository and a reviewer of its publishing environments. If one becomes unavailable, the other two can still close issues, merge changes and release. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity

accessibility_best_practices.justification: This package is a library with no user interface. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

assurance_case.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md states the threat model, the trust boundaries, the secure-design argument and the argument against common implementation weaknesses this criterion asks for. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md

automated_integration_testing.justification: test.yml runs the test suite on every push to main and every pull request, and its aggregate job is a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

build_common_tools.justification: The build uses common tools: uv, hatchling, cffi and CMake, with the platform's C compiler. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md#build

build_floss_tools.justification: The project builds with FLOSS tools alone: uv, hatchling, cffi, CMake and GCC or Clang. Only the static Windows wheels use MSVC. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md#build

build_non_recursive.justification: The vendored build is a single cmake invocation over one CMakeLists.txt tree (scripts/cffi_build.py), not a recursive make over independent subdirectory builds. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/cffi_build.py

build_preserve_debug.justification: CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE set to RelWithDebInfo or Debug builds the vendored library with debug information, and CFLAGS reaches the extension's compile. Release is the default, which every published wheel builds. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/README.md#environment-variables

build_repeatable.justification: wheel-reproducibility.yml builds each platform's wheel twice, for one interpreter, and requires the two archives to match byte for byte, after cibuildwheel's repair step as well. It also builds on a second image per platform, with a different toolchain, and compares the two. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/wheel-reproducibility.yml

build_reproducible.justification: The sdist is built with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH from the commit, and sdist-rebuild.yml rebuilds a release from its signed tag and verifies the rebuilt file against the release's own PyPI attestation; RELEASING.md tells a user how to do the same. Compiled wheels are rebuilt and compared byte for byte by wheel-reproducibility.yml. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/sdist-rebuild.yml

build_standard_variables.justification: Outside Windows, the static extension's compile and link honour CC, CFLAGS, CPPFLAGS, LDSHARED and LDFLAGS as setuptools composes them, as scripts/README.md documents. CMake reads CC and CFLAGS for the vendored library. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/scripts/README.md#environment-variables

bus_factor.justification: fametrano wrote almost all of the code and is the only person who knows it in depth. The claude account in the contributors graph comes from the Co-Authored-By trailer on AI-assisted commits, almost all of them fametrano's. pmazzocchi, an organization owner, did the 2026-09-30 security review and has made only a small change. No person outside the owners has committed to this repository. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. The organization owners administer every repository. Knowledge of the code rests on fametrano alone. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#continuity https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/graphs/contributors

code_of_conduct.justification: btclib-org/.github's CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is this repository's code of conduct, through GitHub's organization-wide default; the community-profile API reports it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

code_review_standards.justification: REVIEWING.md states what a review checks, how a finding is written and what clears a pull request; the part shared by every repository is followed by what this tree checks in particular. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/REVIEWING.md

coding_standards.justification: pyproject.toml selects every ruff rule (select = ["ALL"]) with a documented ignore list, and runs mypy in strict mode. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

coding_standards_enforced.justification: ruff-check, ruff-format and mypy run in .pre-commit-config.yaml, which the required lint check runs on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.pre-commit-config.yaml

contribution_requirements.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding-standard, lint-gate and 100%-coverage requirements a contribution must meet before it can land. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

contributors_unassociated.justification: fametrano is the only significant contributor. pmazzocchi has made only a small change. pmazzocchi and fametrano are associated: both are CheckSig co-founders, as their GitHub profiles state. No person outside the owners has committed to this repository. giacomocaironi, also an organization owner, wrote early parts of the code but has made no commit since 2023. https://github.com/fametrano https://github.com/pmazzocchi

copyright_per_file.justification: Every Python file opens with "Copyright (c) The btclib developers", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/__init__.py

crypto_algorithm_agility.justification: These are bindings to libsecp256k1, which implements one curve, and Bitcoin's consensus rules fix secp256k1, SHA-256 and the signature schemes. Another algorithm needs a soft fork first, and the project follows one when it activates. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

crypto_call.justification: calls libsecp256k1, does not reimplement it

crypto_certificate_verification.justification: This tree performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

crypto_credential_agility.justification: These are bindings with no configuration file or credential store: a secret scalar or nonce is a caller-supplied value or buffer, never read from or written to a file this project owns. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

crypto_keylength.justification: libsecp256k1 has one curve, secp256k1, about 128 bits of security, above NIST's 112-bit floor for 2030. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

crypto_published.justification: FFI bindings to Bitcoin Core's libsecp256k1 (and secp256k1-zkp), which implement published algorithms: ECDSA, BIP340 Schnorr, ECDH

crypto_random.justification: ECDSA nonces are libsecp256k1's RFC 6979; BIP340 aux_rand32, context randomization, the MuSig session secrand and ElligatorSwift entropy default to secrets.token_bytes(32) when the caller supplies none. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/_scalar.py

crypto_tls12.justification: btclib-secp256k1 uses no TLS: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/src/btclib_secp256k1

crypto_used_network.justification: btclib-secp256k1 does not use the network: nothing under src/ imports socket, ssl, http or urllib. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tree/main/src/btclib_secp256k1

crypto_verification_private.justification: This tree performs no network communications and so uses no TLS. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

crypto_weaknesses.justification: The bindings expose libsecp256k1's ECDSA with RFC 6979 nonces, BIP340 Schnorr signatures and BIP327 MuSig2, each SHA-256-based by its specification; there is no caller-configurable cipher and no SHA-1. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/dsa.py

dco.justification: main requires the lint / Sign-off check, which refuses a pull request with a commit that lacks its author's Signed-off-by: trailer. Dependabot's and pre-commit.ci's commits are exempt. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/.github/scripts/check_sign_off.py

delivery_mitm.justification: Distribution channels (GitHub, PyPI) use HTTPS exclusively.

delivery_unsigned.justification: Releases are published to PyPI and GitHub Releases and installed with pip from PyPI, all over HTTPS. No package or hash is fetched over plain HTTP. https://pypi.org/project/btclib-secp256k1/ https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases

dependency_monitoring.justification: Dependabot security updates are on, and Dependabot's weekly version updates cover uv, github-actions, the ClusterFuzzLite image and the vendored libsecp256k1 and secp256k1-zkp submodules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

description_good.justification: btclib-secp256k1 is a set of Python bindings to libsecp256k1, Bitcoin Core's C library for secp256k1. It signs and verifies with ECDSA and BIP340 Schnorr. https://btclib.org/btclib-secp256k1/

discussion.justification: GitHub supports discussions on issues and pull requests.

documentation_achievements.justification: README.md shows the OpenSSF Best Practices badge, linked to this project's page. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

documentation_architecture.justification: ARCHITECTURE.md documents the module layout and layer boundaries of this tree's software. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ARCHITECTURE.md

documentation_current.justification: docs.yml builds the docs with -W -n on every pull request, and the build is a required check. The API reference is generated from the shipped docstrings. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/docs.yml

documentation_quick_start.justification: README.md gives the install command and a Quickstart that tests/examples_test.py runs, so a stale example fails the suite. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

documentation_roadmap.justification: ROADMAP.md, organization-wide in btclib-org/.github, is reviewed every September and states what is maintained, what is intended and what is deliberately not. This repository's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/ROADMAP.md

documentation_security.justification: SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* section states which secret buffers libsecp256k1 zeroizes and which stay in Python objects that cannot be zeroized, the caller-owned `into=` buffers that close part of that gap, and what a scalar's magnitude can leak. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

dynamic_analysis.justification: Every release runs the test suite before it is published. release.yml calls test.yml, and the PyPI upload runs only if it passes. The suite fails below 100% coverage, branches included. ClusterFuzzLite fuzzing and cosmic-ray mutation testing also run every week. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/release.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml

dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions.justification: The test suite runs under pytest with assertions enabled (Python's -O is never used), so every assert in the code and tests is checked on every run. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

dynamic_analysis_fixed.justification: No fuzzing or mutation-testing finding is open, and the weekly fuzz and mutation runs on main pass. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/fuzz.yml https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/mutation.yml

dynamic_analysis_unsafe.justification: This tree vendors and compiles libsecp256k1, C code, and fuzz.yml runs ClusterFuzzLite over the bindings' entry points with sanitizer: address (AddressSanitizer), weekly and on dispatch. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/fuzz.yml

external_dependencies.justification: Every dependency is declared in machine-readable form in pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies] and dependency-groups, resolved and pinned in the committed uv.lock. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

floss_license.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

floss_license_osi.justification: The MIT license is approved by the Open Source Initiative (OSI).

governance.justification: The organization's GOVERNANCE.md documents how decisions are made, the maintainer's bypass and every role. This tree's README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md link it. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md

hardened_site.justification: https://btclib.org/btclib-secp256k1/ is served over HTTPS with Content-Security-Policy (frame-ancestors 'none'), X-Frame-Options: DENY, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Strict-Transport-Security.

hardening.justification: ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules, so a hardening defect such as unsafe deserialization or shell injection fails the lint gate. CodeQL also runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

implement_secure_design.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md's *Secure design principles* section argues how each principle applies to the binding layer, and SECURITY.md's *Limitations of the binding layer* states where that layer stops. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles

input_validation.justification: Each wrapper checks sizes and ranges at the cffi boundary before a pointer reaches C and refuses anything of the wrong length or form; whether the bytes are a valid key, point or signature is left to libsecp256k1, as CONTRIBUTING.md requires. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_common.justification: btclib-secp256k1 is on PyPI, so pip install and pip uninstall install and remove it. README.md gives the command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

installation_development_quick.justification: After git submodule update --init, uv sync --locked installs the whole development environment and builds the extension. CONTRIBUTING.md's *The environment and the gates* gives both. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

installation_standard_variables.justification: Installation is pip install, which follows pip's own install-location conventions; the project has no installer of its own. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

interfaces_current.justification: ruff's UP and FA rules flag deprecated constructs, and pytest turns every warning into an error. deps-latest and deps-oldest run the suite weekly at the newest and the floor versions. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

internationalization.justification: This package is a library and produces no text for end users; its output is bytes and integers. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/README.md

know_common_errors.justification: ASSURANCE_CASE.md argues how each common implementation weakness of a binding layer (CWE-125, 787, 20, 208, 362 and others) is countered in this tree. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#common-implementation-weaknesses

know_secure_design.justification: fametrano, the primary developer, maintains ASSURANCE_CASE.md, whose Secure design principles section applies each principle to this code. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/ASSURANCE_CASE.md#secure-design-principles

license_per_file.justification: Every Python file states "Distributed under the MIT software license, see the accompanying LICENSE file or https://opensource.org/license/mit", e.g. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/src/btclib_secp256k1/__init__.py

maintenance_or_update.justification: Only the latest release is supported and nothing is backported (SECURITY.md). RELEASING.md runs griffe check against the previous tag, and RELEASE_NOTES.md lists what a user must act on to upgrade. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

regression_tests_added50.justification: A merged pull request that changes code under src/ also changes tests/, unless it leaves behaviour as it was: a docstring, a comment, a move, a removal or a refactor. The 100% line and branch coverage gate also fails a fix whose new code no test runs. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates

release_notes_vulns.justification: The release notes name each advisory a release fixes: v0.8.0.10 names GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/RELEASE_NOTES.md

repo_distributed.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git is distributed.

repo_interim.justification: development is on the main branch of https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1

repo_public.justification: Repository on GitHub, which provides public git repositories with URLs.

repo_track.justification: Repository on GitHub, which uses git. git can track the changes, who made them, and when they were made.

report_archive.justification: GitHub Issues and pull requests keep every report and its responses public and searchable. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues?q=is%3Aissue

report_process.justification: Bugs are reported in GitHub Issues, through the bug-report form. CONTRIBUTING.md's The issue tracker says where. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues

report_tracker.justification: Issues are tracked in this repository's GitHub Issues, with issue forms; cross-repository issues go to btclib-org/.github's tracker. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues

require_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication of every member. https://github.com/btclib-org

roles_responsibilities.justification: GOVERNANCE.md's *Roles* describes the maintainer, the owners, repository collaborators, contributors, reviewers, the review bot, Dependabot and pre-commit.ci, and what each owes. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/GOVERNANCE.md#roles

secure_2FA.justification: The btclib-org organization requires two-factor authentication and allows only secure methods: TOTP apps, security keys or passkeys, and GitHub Mobile, not SMS. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/issues/1362#issuecomment-5903994882

security_review.justification: pmazzocchi, an owner other than the maintainer, reviewed the project on 2026-09-30. The review pins its scope to a commit, checks each claim of ASSURANCE_CASE.md, states what it did not cover and files each finding as an issue. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues/1089

signed_releases.justification: Every PyPI file carries a PEP 740 attestation from Trusted Publishing, and every GitHub release from v0.8.0 on a Sigstore provenance bundle. Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on. SECURITY.md gives the verify command. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/releases/latest

sites_password_security.justification: The project runs no site that stores passwords; authentication is GitHub's, PyPI's and Read the Docs'. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

small_tasks.justification: Small tasks for new contributors carry the label "good first issue", which CONTRIBUTING.md sets aside for a first contribution. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/issues?q=label%3A%22good+first+issue%22

static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities.justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request, every push to main and weekly, and ruff's select = ["ALL"] includes the bandit S rules. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_fixed.justification: No static-analysis finding is open: CodeQL has no open alert, and ruff and mypy findings fail the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml

static_analysis_often.justification: on every push and pull request: https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/lint.yml, https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/codeql.yml

test.justification: test.yml runs the pytest suite, gated at 100% line and branch coverage, on every pull request. It checks vectors published by the BIPs and other upstreams, and tests/README.md pins each vendored file to its upstream commit. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/workflows/test.yml

test_branch_coverage80.justification: Branch coverage is measured (branch = true in [tool.coverage.run]) and the 100% gate includes it. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_continuous_integration.justification: test.yml runs the suite on every pull request and push to main. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/actions/workflows/test.yml

test_policy.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md makes 100% coverage a gate every change must pass, so new functionality comes with its tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#the-environment-and-the-gates

test_policy_mandated.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires 100% line and branch coverage, and fail_under = 100 fails the required check on any new code without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

test_statement_coverage80.justification: pyproject.toml sets fail_under = 100 over the Python code, gated on every pull request by test.yml. The vendored C is tested by libsecp256k1's own suite, not by this gate. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

test_statement_coverage90.justification: Coverage is gated at 100% (fail_under = 100 in [tool.coverage.report]) on every pull request. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

tests_are_added.justification: The required check test: every job passed fails any pull request that leaves a line or branch untested. The merged pull requests show recent changes landing with their tests. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged

tests_documented_added.justification: CONTRIBUTING.md documents the 100% coverage gate, so new functionality is not accepted without a test. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md

two_person_review.justification: main's ruleset requires one approving review from somebody other than the author, and fametrano can merge without it through a pull_request-mode bypass. Since 2026-10-14 the bypass is no longer everyday practice. The releases published before that date ship mostly changes merged through it, so fewer than half of what they ship was reviewed by another person. https://github.com/btclib-org/.github/blob/main/README.md#branch-protection-and-rulesets

updateable_reused_components.justification: PyPI packages are pinned in uv.lock and updated by weekly Dependabot pull requests that run the full suite. The vendored libsecp256k1 and secp256k1-zkp are git submodules pinned at a commit, and Dependabot opens a weekly pull request when upstream moves. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml

version_semver.justification: The first three numbers are the bundled libsecp256k1's own version, and a fourth counts releases of the bindings alone on it (0.8.0.1, 0.8.0.2, ...): neither SemVer nor CalVer. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1#readme

version_tags_signed.justification: Release tags are signed from v0.8.0 on, and GitHub verifies each. RELEASING.md signs each tag with git tag -s and reads the signature back after the push. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/tags

vulnerabilities_critical_fixed.justification: No critical vulnerability has been reported; the one advisory (GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c) is medium and was fixed on the day it was published.

vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days.justification: Every published advisory names the release that fixes it, and no Dependabot alert is open. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories

vulnerability_report_credit.justification: The reporter of GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, pmazzocchi, is credited as finder on the advisory. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories/GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c

vulnerability_report_response.justification: GHSA-8h6f-34jj-7p6c, reported privately by pmazzocchi on 2026-09-30, was fixed in v0.8.0.10 and published on 2026-10-03. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/security/advisories

vulnerability_response_process.justification: SECURITY.md's *Reporting a vulnerability* gives the private channels (a GitHub security advisory, or security at btclib dot org) and the response times. Private vulnerability reporting is enabled. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/SECURITY.md

warnings.justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"], mypy with strict = true and pytest with filterwarnings = ["error"], each in a required check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_fixed.justification: Warnings are not tolerated: ruff, strict mypy and pytest's filterwarnings = ["error"] fail the required checks. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml

warnings_strict.justification: ruff runs with select = ["ALL"] and mypy with strict = true, both with zero findings allowed in the required lint check. https://github.com/btclib-org/btclib-secp256k1/blob/main/pyproject.toml
